classification.difficultyReason: Use equal tangent segments, then recognise an auxiliary circle through A,B,T centred at M with AB as diameter to deduce the right angle.

content.prompt: Let AB be a direct common tangent of two circles touching externally. Let the common tangent at the point of contact, T, meet AB at M.

spec.description: Externally touching circles; direct common tangent AB, A,M,B collinear; tangent at T meets AB at M. AT/BT are not supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Original supplied givens and targets only; no derived numerical values or proof conclusions.

answer.worked: Tangents MA and MT from M to the left circle have equal length. Tangents MB and MT from M to the right circle also have equal length. Hence MA=MT=MB.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, deduce that $\angle ATB$ is a right angle.

answer.worked: By part a, A, B and T lie on a circle with centre M and radius MA. Since A,M,B are collinear and MA=MB, AB is a diameter of this circle. Thus $\angle ATB=90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle).
